transcript.answer: The OpenTelemetry metrics API, unlike its tracing API, has no proxy meter. An instrument created from `metrics.getMeter()` before a `MeterProvider` is registered is therefore a permanent no-op. It stays a no-op even if a provider is registered later. Lore hit this in `libs/server-core/src/outbound/otel.ts`, which created its instruments at import time. The entrypoint imported that file before `initOtel()` ran, so `lore.http.requests`, `lore.tool.calls` and the other counters never recorded anything. The fix, in PR #2652 and ADR-050, moved the instruments to `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts`. They are now resolved lazily against the provider registered at record time, and each lookup is memoized per provider.

judgements.reason: The answer states that the metrics API has no proxy meter, that instruments created before provider registration stay permanent no-ops, and that Lore now resolves instruments lazily against the current provider, matching all essentials of the gold answer.
